purpose: Deterministic offline fixtures for classified research participation, compartment integration, capability observation, partial compromise, declassification/reclassification, and bounded long-run security state. They are design/CI guardrails, not final balance promises.

scenarios.description: A classified stealth-detection program has substantial polity research capacity, but only authorized labs/experts can participate. Slower progress comes from real eligible capacity, not a secrecy multiplier.
assertions: eligible classified capacity equals real authorized capacity
unauthorized labs contribute zero
classification itself does not modify RP efficiency

scenarios.description: A field-defense engineering program splits theory, prototype, manufacturing, and control records into compartments. Engineering cannot integrate the design until an authorized integration context can access the necessary compartments.
assertions: missing compartment access creates a concrete blocker
adding real authorized integration access removes the blocker
no generic compartment research penalty is used

scenarios.description: A classified field-defense implementation is used in combat. A foreign observer legitimately detects its effect but acquires no implementation records.
assertions: classification cannot hide a genuinely observed physical effect
observation creates capability evidence without implementation records
observation does not reveal the source research node to the observer by fiat

scenarios.description: A foreign actor acquires a classified antimatter-containment dataset and engineering blueprints but no production tooling, operating institution, expert cohort, or training pipeline.
assertions: partial records improve foreign assessment
missing tooling and experts limit reproduction
stolen records do not automatically make the native node Mature
owner does not automatically know the recipient unless compromise detection established it

scenarios.description: A mature technology is known in two classified research contexts. Declassification authorizes four additional synchronized contexts, which receive codified records through normal communications and create more independent archive copies.
assertions: declassification does not alter scientific maturity
newly authorized contexts still wait for real record delivery
additional copies improve archive resilience
practice does not appear automatically with records

scenarios.description: A previously normal scientific record exists as codified copies in four contexts. The polity reclassifies future dissemination to two contexts; policy stops future normal sharing but does not physically erase the two already distributed copies.
assertions: reclassification affects future access/dissemination policy
already distributed records remain until real deletion/recovery actions occur
classification policy is not a physical recall mechanism

scenarios.description: Reference 1,000-year security-state workload. Most research remains normal scientific access and therefore has no explicit security record.
rules: default normal-scientific access creates no per-node security record
declassified records return to normal state and delete redundant policy rows
compartment membership uses groups rather than people
known compromise detail compresses after strategic relevance fades
security records never duplicate the technology graph
